title: Fasting days (Didache 8)
hookLine: fast on Wednesdays and Fridays, and pray the Lord's Prayer three times a day
tomorrow: where would you look for a sermon with no words in it?

cards: Sunday night, a phone on the kitchen counter. Someone is setting up the week. Two days get a small circle: Wednesday, Friday.
Three alarms go in, every day, each with the same one-word label: pause. A roommate glances over and guesses a medicine schedule. It isn't.
It's a rhythm out of a short book that churches have handed down, and it fits on one screen.

teach.b: The book is the Didache, and chapter eight is short and practical. Fast, it says, on the fourth day and on the day of Preparation: Wednesday and Friday. Then it turns to prayer.
Pray as the Lord commanded in his Gospel, it says, and it writes out the Lord's Prayer, the one Jesus teaches in Matthew: "Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name."
The Didache's version ends in praise: for yours is the power and the glory forever. Then the instruction: pray this three times a day. That rhythm has older roots.
In the book of Daniel, the prophet "kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God." A psalm says, "Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray."
The Didache takes that old rhythm and sets the Lord's Prayer inside it. What strikes some readers is how ordinary it all is. Two days a week with less food.
A faith with a calendar and a clock, built into weeks that otherwise look like anyone else's.
Nothing here asks for a mountaintop. It asks for Wednesday.

how: Some Christians still keep Wednesday and Friday as fasting days, and many pray at set hours, morning, noon and evening, often with the Lord's Prayer.

games.why: Didache 8 asks for the Lord's Prayer three times a day: a few lines, said often, built into an ordinary day.

practice: Turn your phone face down and slide it out of reach for the length of the sit: a small fast, right now.
If a Wednesday fast appeals to you, choose only what's safe for your body, a snack, a coffee, your phone at lunch; anyone who shouldn't skip food can fast from something else.
